body_html:
Two or three weeks is an awkward stay: longer than a week, shorter than a month. The obvious answer is to chain weekly blocks, but with the reference prices the shop has confirmed that is not always the cheapest way, because the monthly reference price is far lower than four weekly ones. The arithmetic takes five minutes, and it points to a handful of questions that only the shop can answer.

What the reference prices say

The shop's reference prices for a manual bike, at Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà, are 700,000 to 800,000 VND a week and 1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND a month. These are reference ranges, so confirm the bike and the rate when you book. At these prices a month costs roughly as much as 1.25 to 1.7 weeks: 1,000,000 ÷ 800,000 at the cheapest end and 1,200,000 ÷ 700,000 at the dearest. That means two weekly blocks already cost more than a whole month. The table rounds each stay up to whole weekly blocks and sets them against the full monthly price:

StayWeekly blocksCost of the blocksFull monthMonth is cheaper by
8 to 14 days21,400,000 to 1,600,000 VND1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND200,000 to 600,000 VND
15 to 21 days32,100,000 to 2,400,000 VND1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND900,000 to 1,400,000 VND
22 to 28 days42,800,000 to 3,200,000 VND1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND1,600,000 to 2,200,000 VND

The comparison is deliberately harsh on the month: it assumes you pay the full monthly price even if you hand the bike back after two or three weeks. On those reference ranges the month still comes out cheaper. For an automatic bike the picture is less clear. Its weekly range is 600,000 to 1,000,000 VND and its monthly range 1,200,000 to 2,000,000 VND, so two weekly blocks (1,200,000 to 2,000,000 VND) cover exactly the same range as the month, and only the exact figures for your bike can settle it.

For 8 to 10 days the table overstates the month's lead, because one week plus a few single days can cost less than two weekly blocks. For example, adding single days at the manual day rate of 150,000 to 200,000 VND gives 700,000 + 150,000 = 850,000 VND up to 800,000 + 200,000 = 1,000,000 VND for a week and one day, and 1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND for a week and two days.

For example, a 20-day stay by weekly blocks means three blocks, 2,100,000 to 2,400,000 VND, against a single month at 1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND. The month saves at least 900,000 VND even though about ten of its days go unused, and that gap is the number to keep in mind when you hear the shop's answer on early return.

The questions that decide it

The table is only a starting point, because it rests on assumptions about how a monthly booking works. Ask the shop:

  • Can I book the monthly rate for a stay shorter than a month?
  • Is there a minimum rental period for the monthly rate?
  • If I return the bike early, is any part of the monthly price refunded, credited or kept? Do not assume either answer.
  • Which bike do the weekly and monthly figures refer to?
  • If I keep the bike past the end date, how is the extension charged? The shop's confirmed fee is 20,000 VND per hour, and more than 6 hours counts as one rental day; ask whether that rule changes under a monthly booking.

Write the answers down. If the shop's answer on early return turns out to be the worst case, in which you pay the whole month, compare that figure with your weekly blocks as the table does; at the reference prices it is often still the cheaper option.

A message you can send

The copy-and-send booking message covers the general request; a short message that adds the week and month questions gets all of this answered at once: "Hello, I will be in Hanoi for about [number] days from [date], and I would like a [manual or automatic] bike. What would [two or three] weekly blocks cost, and what is the monthly price? If I return the bike after [number] days, how is the monthly price treated? Please confirm the bike and the rate before I book." Replace the square brackets with your details and keep the reply where you can find it again.

When the month is not the answer

  • You will ride only a few days. A long hold only makes sense if you will ride most days; otherwise day-by-day or one weekly block may be enough.
  • You cannot keep the bike somewhere safe. A bike you hold for weeks needs a secure place at night, and parking fees count against the saving.
  • Your stay may end much sooner. If there is a real chance you will leave early, the shop's early return answer matters more than the arithmetic.
  • The quote says otherwise. The reference range is a range; your exact quote may put the week and the month closer together.

Beyond the price: living with a bike for weeks

Holding a bike for two or three weeks is a small version of a monthly rental, so the same routines help: knowing when to check the tyres and lights, and tracking fuel so you notice anything unusual. The guide to a monthly rental maintenance visit calendar and the guide to tracking fuel use on a monthly Hanoi rental both apply. The shop's monthly motorbike rental in Hanoi page describes the longer rental, and more guides are in the Weekly & Monthly Rentals category.
